outcome: duration of first stage of labor
cohort: 150 primigravida women randomly divided into two groups: those who were allowed a female companion of their choice (n=75) and those who received routine care without a companion (n=75)
finding: Birth companionship during labor was associated with increased spontaneous vaginal births, a trend toward shorter first stage labor duration, decreased need for labor augmentation, and higher maternal satisfaction and early breastfeeding initiation.
mod_finding: The study found a significantly higher rate of spontaneous vaginal births among women who had a birth companion compared to those who did not.
